headline: Qualcomm Unveils Snapdragon Reality Elite Chip for Next-Gen AR
summary: New chip promises up to 160% NPU performance boost, enabling powerful on-device AI for AR glasses and other wearables.
details: Qualcomm is betting big on a future beyond smartphones, announcing its new Snapdragon Reality Elite platform for mixed reality glasses. This new chip aims to power more advanced on-device AI capabilities for augmented reality devices and a wide range of other AI-powered wearables.

The Snapdragon Reality Elite platform offers significant performance improvements over its predecessor, with up to 60% faster GPU, 30% faster CPU, and a massive 160% boost in NPU performance. This allows for AI models with up to 3 billion parameters to run at 45 tokens per second, enabling responsive AI interactions.

Beyond raw performance, the new platform enhances head and hand tracking for more intuitive control and offers improved see-through capabilities for AR glasses. It supports a 4.4K per-eye resolution at 90 fps, contributing to a smoother and more comfortable visual experience, crucial for reducing motion sickness.

Qualcomm is also introducing the Scalable Turnkey AI-Ready Toolkit (START), a comprehensive package of hardware and software designed to accelerate the development of AI devices, starting with smart glasses. This includes reference designs for various form factors.

The START toolkit aims to lower the barrier to entry for hardware manufacturers, with initial partners like Inspecs and O’Neill set to leverage its white-label program. Qualcomm envisions START expanding to support numerous AI wearable form factors beyond just glasses in the future.

Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon highlighted the company's work on over 40 different AI wearable device designs, ranging from jewelry to smartwatches. He believes these devices, designed to be worn constantly and interact with the environment, represent the next major computing platform after the smartphone.
